Issued at 123 AM CDT Sat Aug 15 2026

A shortwave trough is pivoting across eastern IA and northern 
MO and will eventually traverse across northern IL and northwest
IN later tonight into Saturday morning. Ahead of the wave, 
isolated to widely scattered showers and sprinkles continue to 
fester over IL and IN but with the very limited forcing and 
instability their intensity is meager to say the least. Closer 
to the shortwave, however, an axis of thunderstorms is 
developing near the IA-MO border along a remnant outflow 
boundary from last night's storms. These storms are expected to 
become more widespread in coverage and spread east across north-
central IL and northwest IN through the night and will linger 
into Saturday morning. Given the near record PWATs (around 2.5 
inches) in conjunction with modest instability, a developing 
low-level jet, and the aforementioned wave, conditions are 
favorable for torrential rainfall (rain rates of 2+ in/hr) to 
occur with these storms. While most of northern IL and northwest
IN is expected to see showers and storms tonight, a localized 
axis is expected to see the highest rainfall amounts. At this 
time, the axis of heaviest rainfall looks to be setting up near 
and south of a Peru, IL to Rensselaer, IN line but as storm 
coverage expands cannot rule out this axis shifting a hair 
northward towards I-80. Regardless, rainfall amounts within the 
heaviest axis look to be in excess of 3- 4 inches which given 
the saturated soils and elevated river levels from previous days
of rain could lead to significant flash flooding. For this 
reason a higher-end Flood Watch remains in effect for areas 
south of I-80 through 10 AM CDT Saturday to highlight this 
threat. 

Outside of this heavier rain axis, heavy downpours are still 
expected with the showers and storms tonight but with the lower 
likelihood of training convection the flood threat looks to be 
more localized to poor drainage and lower-lying areas for those 
north of I-80. Nevertheless, a Flood Watch remains in effect for
our IL counties between I-88 and I-80 through 10 AM CDT. 
Additionally, resent mesoanalysis does show around 30-35 kts of 
effective shear overhead which may support a few storms becoming
stronger. While the overall threat for widespread severe 
weather looks low due to the poor lapse rates and modest 
instability present, locally gusty winds upwards of 40-45 mph 
cannot be ruled out with the stronger storms tonight. 

As we head into this afternoon, the aforementioned shortwave 
will exit the area and allow any lingering showers and 
thunderstorms to diminish in coverage and push east of the area.
Overall it looks as if most of the afternoon hours Saturday 
should be dry for most, but forecast soundings do show some 
lingering moisture in the presence of weakly unstable air which 
may support some isolated showers festering across parts of the 
area through sunset. With some broad synoptic ascent forecast to
be overhead Saturday, it is hard to pin point any specific 
areas showers will be favored so have opted to just keep all of 
northern IL and northwest IN under some 15% POPs for now. 
Otherwise, expect mostly cloudy skies to prevail through the day
though temperatures should still be able to warm into the lower
to mid-80s with continued warm advection. 

Another shortwave trough is expected to pivot across the 
Mississippi River Valley tonight with a cold front in tow. These
features look to lead to the development of additional showers 
and thunderstorms across northern IL and northwest IN late this 
evening into the overnight hours. Initially the coverage of 
shower/storms along the front may be more muted as our area 
resides in the subsidence behind this afternoon's wave and the 
new one tonight, but coverage should increase overnight as the 
front progresses southward. With the humid air mass still in 
place in combination with the modest instability and forcing, 
these showers/storms will once again be capable of locally heavy
to torrential downpours. However, since the front should be 
rather progressive it seems the threat for training storms and 
flooding should be lower. Finally, there will also be another 
threat for locally gusty winds with the storms tonight though 
the overall severe threat does look low. 

The cold front is expected to just about exit our area by 
Sunday morning which will allow drier air to filter in and 
finally conclude this active pattern. However, there is a chance
that some isolated showers or storms may attempt to develop 
near the front Sunday afternoon south and east of I-57, but with
the drier air and capping confidence is low on showers/storms 
actually materializing. Therefore, expect most areas to be dry 
for Sunday afternoon with temperatures still seasonable in the 
lower to mid-80s. Winds will be out of the northwest with gusts 
peaking around 20 mph during the afternoon.
